title: Guelph woman haunted by memories of shooting victim
article: Lesley Dickieson says she has been haunted by the shooting death of Brandon Duncan, and feels the 36-year-old homeless man was let down by the mental health care system.

Duncan was shot and killed on May 20 during an interaction with two Guelph Police officers while he was inside the Guelph General Hospital's emergency department. The Ontario Special Investigations Unit has assigned 12 investigators to probe the incident to determine if there was wrongdoing on the part of police.

Dickieson said she had a heartrending encounter with Duncan last November on a cold evening that left a lasting impression. The 45-year-old personal support worker said she was out on the town with friends and needed cash. She stepped into the Royal Bank in downtown Guelph and saw Duncan, who was crouched on the floor, struggling with a leaky colostomy bag, homeless and in distress.
"This whole thing is just sickening and it's haunting me. I just can't seem to let it go," Dickieson said Friday in a telephone interview.

"There were so many people going into the bank machine and coming out, and there he was on the floor in the corner," she said. "I immediately asked him, 'Are you OK honey?' And he said, 'No.' I asked him if he needed help and he said that he did."
Duncan was in pain, and he told Dickieson he had nowhere to go. The man suffered from Crohn's disease and had several surgeries related to his illness in the past.

"His colostomy bag exploded and it was leaking everywhere," Dickieson said, adding that Duncan did not have the necessary medical supplies to remedy the situation, and clearly could not afford those supplies.

"People were walking in and saying, 'Oh my God, that's so disgusting.' And they would just walk away," Dickieson said. "We were astonished at how many people came and went and didn't offer to help him."
Dickieson said she and her friends called 911 and waited with the man until paramedics arrived. While sitting with Duncan, Dickieson learned just how desperate and helpless he was, she said.

"The way that the situation went down at the Guelph General Hospital is not the person we encountered at the Royal Bank," she added. "The guy I saw at the Royal Bank, he was scared, he was alone, he was embarrassed, and he just needed somebody, anyone, to just say, 'it's OK, it's going to be OK.'"

40 Baker Street, an agency housing several programs for the homeless, is dedicating its Monday evening pizza dinner to Duncan, a man who struggled for many years with mental illness, addiction, health problems and homelessness, those close to him said this week.

A memorial service is also being planned. Rev. Anne Gajerski-Cauley said Friday she is organizing a memorial for Duncan because the shooting victim should not go without a dignified memorial service. Gajerski-Cauley is a local United Church minister and the federal New Democratic Party candidate for Wellington-Halton Hills.

"I was concerned that I wasn't hearing anything from the faith community initially around what had happened," Gajerski-Cauley said. She said she spoke to officials at Wall-Custance Funeral Home and Chapel at 206 Norfolk St. in Guelph, which has donated space the service Thursday, June 4, beginning at 7 p.m.
Gajerski-Cauley said personnel at Guelph General Hospital and Guelph Police Service are likely in a state of shock over the shooting. She wants to invite them to the memorial service.
"Nothing liturgical has happened yet," she said. "I want to do an actual memorial service."
She said it is important for people who knew Duncan and/or were affected by his death to worship, grieve and commemorate the man together. The entire community is impacted by this tragedy, she said.
"If they feel a need for some sort of closure on this, because this has impacted the whole community, they should come to the memorial," she said. "That includes people who are homeless."
Gajerski-Cauley said the deceased man's body will not be present at the memorial service, since it is unknown when Duncan's body will be released by the Special Investigations Unit for burial.
